title: SDK Neutralization Registry Entry
description: Defines which public API methods of a third-party SDK can be safely neutralized (stubbed) in a decompiled Android APK.

sdk_id.description: Unique lowercase identifier for this SDK. Equals the file name stem, except consent-umptcf.json -> google-ump-consent (historical). Consumers always use sdk_id, never the file name.

display_name.description: Human-readable SDK name. Must not contain ':', '|', tab or newline (registry-scan.py and neutralize.sh use ':' and '|' as separators).

known_versions.description: SDK versions tested against (for reference only)

in_house_wrapper.description: True when this entry is a publisher's own in-house ad/analytics mediation wrapper (it calls third-party network SDKs, or serves house/WebView ads, on the app's behalf) rather than a third-party SDK. Metadata only: registry-scan.py ignores it; detect-adwrapper.sh uses it so it does NOT treat this package as a known third-party SDK to exclude, and can flag the app as carrying an in-house wrapper.

packages.description: Root Java/Kotlin packages of this SDK

internal_prefix.description: If known, the obfuscation prefix pattern (e.g. 'zz', single letters)

targets.description: OPTIONAL. ABSENT = detection-only entry: registry-scan.py and neutralize.sh ignore it completely (a detection-only entry must not carry manifest_components or protected_patterns). Never null.

entry_points.description: Level 1: SDK init methods. Stubbing these disables the entire SDK.

ad_operations.description: Level 2: load/show/cache methods. Safety net if init stub is bypassed.

deep_patterns.description: Level 3: Broad internal patterns. Use for well-known SDK internals.

protected_patterns.description: Methods/patterns that must NEVER be stubbed in this SDK

detection.description: Facts for the AUDIT only (find-trackers / find-ads). NEVER read by registry-scan.py or neutralize.sh and, in step 1, not by detect-adwrapper either: nothing here changes what gets neutralized. No regex anywhere: literals only.

extra_packages.description: Identity packages NOT (yet) in `packages`: legacy, sub-products, code only this SDK ships. Each item is by definition a 'detected but not neutralized' gap. Disjoint from `packages`.

exclude_packages.description: Sub-packages of this entry's own roots that do NOT prove this SDK (e.g. gms.ads.identifier for google-admob, com.facebook.ads for facebook).

namespace_roots.description: Wider vendor namespaces: code under them is LIBRARY (never app code), NEVER identity. Shared namespaces are forbidden (lint L12).

adapter_packages.description: Mediators only: where the adapters to other networks live (one sub-package per network).

marker_classes.description: Public top-level classes (no '$') verified on a real APK. When declared and none is present, the code found counts as MEDIUM (PARTIAL), not HIGH.

apis.description: Class-qualified APIs, in addition to the ones derived automatically from targets. A bare method name is never evidence.

domains.description: Hosts or registrable suffixes (braze.com covers sdk.iad-01.braze.com). Weak evidence (LOW).

manifest_names.description: Exact android:name values (meta-data, permission, action, component) that identify the SDK and do NOT start with one of its roots (those are matched by prefix automatically). Evidence only, never disabled.

id_prefixes.description: Literal id prefixes (e.g. ca-app-pub- with label admob_id); no regex.

method_target.description: A method to neutralize. Provide EITHER 'stub' (replace body with a trivial no-op/constant return, derived from the return type by neutralize.sh) OR 'inject' (replace body with a purpose-built code sequence that actively does something — see 'inject'). 'inject' takes precedence over 'stub'.

signature.description: Smali-style signature or '*' for all overloads

stub.description: Trivial stub type. neutralize.sh actually derives the concrete stub from the method's smali return type; this field documents intent.

inject.description: CODE INJECTION (distinct from 'stub': the replacement body actively executes logic, it does not merely return). Kinds: 'consent-reject-all' — for the static void UMP form-show entry point loadAndShowConsentFormIfRequired(Activity,OnConsentFormDismissedListener): writes IAB TCF v2.2 reject-all values (gdprApplies=1, all-zero consent/LI keys, reject-all TCString) to the DEFAULT SharedPreferences, then invokes the passed OnConsentFormDismissedListener.onConsentFormDismissed(null) so the app proceeds as if the user chose 'reject all' — the dialog is never shown. 'consent-info-update-success' — for the instance void requestConsentInfoUpdate(Activity,ConsentRequestParameters,OnConsentInfoUpdateSuccessListener,OnConsentInfoUpdateFailureListener): immediately fires the success listener (no network) so the app continues its consent flow. 'return-const-1' / 'return-const-3' — return a fixed int/boolean constant (used to make canRequestAds()=true and getConsentStatus()=OBTAINED(3), so the app treats consent as handled and never re-shows the form). These target the concrete (often obfuscated, version-specific) UMP ConsentInformation implementation.

rule.description: How aggressively to stub matched classes

pattern.description: Glob or regex pattern for methods to protect
